uncited: **Inputs:** Sparse input images or partial 3DGS data containing large occlusions.
**Outputs:** A set of 3D Gaussians with optimized attributes (position, covariance, opacity, spherical harmonics coefficients).
*   **3D Gaussian Set:** A collection of $N$ Gaussians.
*   Covariance matrix $\Sigma_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$ (often parameterized by rotation $R_i \in SO(3)$ and scale $s_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$).
*   Spherical Harmonics coefficients $c_{i,lm}$ for color/diffuse appearance.
*   **ControlNet:** A pre-trained diffusion model encoder/decoder structure conditioned on input images, fine-tuned for this task.
**Visual Hull Initialization:** Generate an initial set of 3D Gaussians constrained within the visual hull derived from the input views.
**Attribute Noise Injection:** To create training data for the repair network, add noise to the attributes of the initialized Gaussians.
**Rendering:** Render the noisy Gaussians from the input viewpoints to produce degraded images.
**ControlNet Fine-Tuning:** Fine-tune a pre-trained ControlNet [101] to map the degraded rendered images back to clean, high-quality representations.
**Optimization:** Update the Gaussian attributes using the repaired outputs from the ControlNet.

*   **Degenerate Input:** Performance relies on the quality of the visual hull; severe occlusions may require robust diffusion priors to hallucinate plausible geometry.

*   **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources.
*   **Limitations:** Relies on a pre-trained diffusion model, which may introduce hallucinated details not present in the input data.
